title: Repo Governor governance manifest, version 1
$comment: Canonical format is JSON (ADR-015). This schema is the specification; the YAML in reference/onboarding.md §21 is illustration. The manifest binds providers to roles and states permissions. It must never carry provider state (§21).

version.$comment: Schema version. An engine encountering a version it does not implement refuses to evaluate rather than guessing (ADR-004 rule 4).

enforcement.$comment: ADR-029 decision 3: enforcement is opt-in PER REPOSITORY, and absent means advisory -- an un-onboarded repository is not a governed one, and blocking there would stop all editing wherever the manifest is absent. Read only by tools/hooks/governance-hook.py; the engine never reads it and gains no capability from it. AN ENUM, NOT A STRING, because the hook compares mode == "blocking": a typo would fall through to advisory and give a repository weaker governance than it declared, silently, which is exactly the defect issue 189 fixed one layer down. docs/installation.md documented this key while additionalProperties refused it, so following the instructions produced MANIFEST_INVALID and every verdict degraded to UNKNOWN (issue 198).

floor_reason.$comment: Set when an indicator raised the floor (ADR-006). A floor may not be overridden downward.

override_active.$comment: True when a human set a level above the floor. Surfaced in every decision record it affects.

providers.$comment: Cardinality per ADR-013: roles that answer 'is this authorized?' are single-valued; evidence roles accumulate.

permissions.$comment: Deny by default (ADR-005). An unlisted role, an unlisted verb, or a malformed block resolves to deny. There is no sensible-default branch.

adapter.$comment: Explicit path, repository-relative. Implicit adapter discovery would reintroduce the silent-binding problem INV-013 forbids (ADR-004 rule 6).

env.$comment: Adapter-specific configuration, passed verbatim to the adapter process (ADR-021). It exists so the ENGINE never has to know an adapter's variable names -- the alternative was `if adapter == 'adapters/linear'` in engine code, which is a binding decision made in code. Credentials must NOT appear here: the secret scan covers this object like any other, and ADR-005 rule 3 keeps credentials in the environment where the manifest cannot record them.

transport.$comment: Declared, never inferred (ADR-016 rule 3). Defaulting to MCP because a server happens to be connected is INV-014 in a different costume.

permission.$comment: Closed verb set. 'execute' is reserved and rejected at v1 (ADR-005 rule 6) because listing it without semantics invites divergent interpretation.

admission.$comment: ADR-018: declared, never assumed. No fallback chain -- trying Projects then milestones then labels would be the adapter deciding what admission means in someone else's repository.
